#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script> -- <ARRAY_JOB_ID> <ARRAY_TASK_ID>

# Slurm resources:
#   --time=01:00:00
#   -n 1
#   -p gpu2
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   -o resnet50-bs128_%A_%a.log
#   --mem-per-cpu=8000

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=1h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=8000
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p gpu2 (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on non-GPU nodes or have different limits/priority (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: -o with %A/%a tokens
# Slurm tokens %A (array master job id) and %a (array index) are not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Slurm variables $SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID and $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID are not set under Flux.
# Accept them as positional arguments.
ARRAY_JOB_ID=${1:-0}
ARRAY_TASK_ID=${2:-0}

cd /home/steinba/development/deeprace/
pwd

module load modenv/both modenv/eb tensorflow/1.3.0-Python-3.5.2 docopt/0.6.2 keras/2.1.4 h5py/2.6.0-intel-2016.03-GCC-5.3-Python-3.5.2-HDF5-1.8.17-serial

python3 ./deeprace.py train -O batch_size=128 -c "k80:1,fs:nfs" \
  -t /home/steinba/development/deeprace/scripts/short/resnet56v1-short-bs128-${ARRAY_JOB_ID}_${ARRAY_TASK_ID}.tsv \
  -e 15 resnet56v1

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=8000`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM.

The original Slurm job specified a GPU partition (`-p gpu2`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
